_copyLayers: 'headline', 'subheadline', 'description' and 'body' fields are Layer 1 — plain language a non-technical, non-native English reader understands in one pass. 'alsoCalled' is Layer 2: the industry/AI term for the same thing, so search and LLMs match it without the human having to decode it. Keep Layer 3 vocabulary (framework and architecture names) in JSON-LD, llms.txt, and the project pages.

hero.headline: How working together goes
hero.subheadline: What I can build for you, what happens week by week, and the answers to the questions people ask me most.

intro.title: What I actually build
intro.body: I do not choose projects by the tools involved. Tell me what you want to exist, and I will tell you the shortest honest way to get there. If your project needs a designer, a tester, or a server specialist, I bring in people I have worked with before — and you still deal with one person.

outcomes.title: The first real version of your product
outcomes.description: From an idea you have already thought through, to something real customers can use — in about 6 to 8 weeks. Phone app, website, admin screen, and the server behind it.
outcomes.bestFor: You know what you want and you need it working, without hiring a whole team.

outcomes.title: A phone app
outcomes.alsoCalled: iOS and Android mobile app, Flutter development
outcomes.description: One app that works on both iPhone and Android, built once instead of twice. Works without internet where it needs to, and feels as fast as any other app on the phone.
outcomes.bestFor: You need to be on people's phones without paying to build the same app twice.

outcomes.title: Making it handle more people
outcomes.description: Taking something that works for a hundred users and making it work for a hundred thousand — faster, cheaper to run, and with alarms that tell you about problems before your customers do.
outcomes.bestFor: You already have customers, and growth is starting to break things.

outcomes.title: Adding AI to what you already have
outcomes.alsoCalled: GenAI features, LLM integration, RAG, chatbot
outcomes.description: A real AI feature inside your product — answering questions from your own documents, summarising, sorting, or chatting with customers. Built with controls on what it costs, how fast it answers, and how often it is right.
outcomes.bestFor: You want AI that actually works in your product, not a demo that impresses once.

outcomes.title: A website that does real work
outcomes.description: Not a brochure — a website people log into and get things done in, with a proper database behind it. Built so it can be maintained for years, by me or by anyone after me.
outcomes.bestFor: Marketplaces, business tools, internal systems — anything past a marketing page.

outcomes.title: Rescuing a project that went wrong
outcomes.alsoCalled: project rescue, technical audit, legacy takeover
outcomes.description: An honest look at what has been built so far, and a straight answer about where it stands. Then a plan to finish it. I can do the work, or hand the plan to your own team.
outcomes.bestFor: Your project is late, over budget, breaking in front of customers, or your developer left.

steps.label: You write to me
steps.description: One or two lines about what you want. Use the form or email. I reply within 24 hours on working days.

steps.label: We talk
steps.description: 30 minutes. You explain, I ask questions, and I tell you what I think the risks are. No sales pitch.

steps.label: I send a plan
steps.description: Within 2 to 3 days: what gets built, in what order, how long it takes, and the price of each stage in writing.

steps.label: I build it
steps.description: You see working progress every week. Short updates in between. The code sits in your own account from day one.

steps.label: It goes live
steps.description: Published and running for real users, with written instructions and a plan for what comes next.

notFor.title: When I am not the right choice
items: You change what you want every week. I price work in stages, and a stage has to be decided before it starts.
You want one final price for everything before anyone has looked at it properly. I price each stage, not the whole project unseen.
You are looking for the cheapest option. I am not the cheapest and I will not pretend to be.

finalCta.headline: Tell me what you want to build.
finalCta.body: Send a few lines — what it is, roughly what you can spend, and when you need it. I will tell you honestly whether I can help and what I think the sensible next step is.
